title: Lord, Have Mercy When We Pray
description: Lord, Have Mercy When We Pray in Tonic Solfa to HOLLINGSIDE, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Hart Milman wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 204, “Lord, Have Mercy”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens Double (7.7.7.7 D) (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HOLLINGSIDE; any other Sevens Double (7.7.7.7 D) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, have mer-cy when we pray Strength to seek a bet-ter way; When our wak-ening thoughts be-gin First to loathe their cher-ished sin; When our wea-ry spi-rits fail, And our a-ching brows are pale; Then Thy strength-ening grace af-ford; Then, O, then, have mer-cy, Lord!

lines: Lord, have mercy when we pray
Strength to seek a better way;
First to loathe their cherished sin;
And our aching brows are pale;
Then, O, then, have mercy, Lord!
Lord, have mercy when we know
First how vain this world below;
When the earliest gleam is given
Of the bright but distant heaven;
Then, O, then, have mercy, Lord!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Henry Hart Milman died in 1868.
credits: Words by Henry Hart Milman (1791–1868), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to HOLLINGSIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
